purpose: Malaysia official rent series for four-quadrant v1 test 1 (implied rent growth g* = r_f + rho - R/P) and for forward-ledger entry 004 (F1 suspended-supply valve proposition). The primary series is DOSM CPI COICOP 041 "Actual rentals for housing", the ONLY official, non-asking, repeat-frequency rent measure published for Malaysia.
discipline: Every value is transcribed from an official DOSM file (parquet from storage.dosm.gov.my, cross-checked against the DOSM monthly CPI release xlsx). Nothing is interpolated, estimated, smoothed, backcast, spliced by us, or sourced from a listing/asking platform. Where a series does not exist (KL-level rent, high-rise rent, net rent) the field is null with a stated reason, never a proxy.

publication.series: Consumer Price Index Malaysia / Indeks Harga Pengguna Malaysia
publication.publisher: Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) / Jabatan Perangkaan Malaysia
publication.referenceBaseVerified: DOSM monthly release xlsx table titles read "Indeks Harga Pengguna (2010=100)" as of the June 2026 release; OpenDOSM cpi_4d catalogue field description reads "[Float] Index value, with base 2010 = 100". As of 2026-06 DOSM has NOT rebased the published CPI to 2020=100.
publication.frequency: monthly (publication); effective repricing frequency of the rent series is QUARTERLY — see repricingCadence
publication.classification: COICOP 2018 from the January 2024 release onward; COICOP 1999 (4-digit) before that — see seriesBreaks
publication.imputedRent: ABSENT. Malaysia CPI has no COICOP 042 (imputed rentals for housing). Division 04 therefore covers only actual rents paid by tenants plus maintenance, water and energy. Owner-occupier housing cost does not enter Malaysian CPI.

cpi_041_national.code: 041 (= 0411 = 04110, identical values at all three digit levels)
cpi_041_national.leaf_bm: Sewa sebenar yang dibayar oleh penyewa
cpi_041_national.caliber: average rent of the CONTINUING stock of tenancies priced by DOSM enumerators; it is a stock-of-contracts rent, not a new-letting/spot rent. Gross rent, not net of management fee, tax, vacancy or collection loss.
cpi_041_national.dwellingTypeSplitReason: DOSM publishes 041 as a single expenditure class down to 5 digits (04110). There is no terraced/high-rise/serviced-apartment breakdown at any published digit level.

cpi_04_national.bm: Perumahan, Air, Elektrik, Gas & Bahan Api Lain
cpi_04_national.en: Housing, Water, Electricity, Gas & Other Fuels
cpi_04_national.note: Division aggregate. Contains 041 (w 17.7) + 043 (1.2) + 044 (1.2) + 045 (3.1). NOT a rent index — the 045 energy component is administered-price driven and moves independently of rent.

cpi_043_national.en: Maintenance, repair & security of the dwelling
cpi_043_national.note: Included because 04320/04441 (maintenance charges in multi-occupied buildings) is the closest official series to strata holding cost h in the Lambda mechanism of four-quadrant v1 section 3.

cpi_044_national.bm: Bekalan air & pelbagai perkhidmatan berkaitan kediaman
cpi_044_national.en: Water supply & miscellaneous services relating to the dwelling

cpi_045_national.note: Diagnostic series. Fell 107.4 (2019-12) to 76.8 (2020-06) on the COVID electricity bill discount and has never returned to the pre-2020 level (97.4 at 2026-06). This single component is why every state-level division-04 index shows a 2020 decline that has nothing to do with rent.

cpi_overall_national.note: Supplied so real rent growth can be computed without importing a second source.

cpi_04_kl.en: Housing, Water, Electricity, Gas & Other Fuels — Kuala Lumpur
cpi_04_kl.WARNING: This is the FINEST geographic cut DOSM publishes for housing, and it is a DIVISION aggregate, not a rent index. It cannot be converted to a KL rent index: DOSM does not publish state-level sub-division weights, so the energy/water components cannot be stripped out. Its 2020 negative YoY (-1.96% at 2020-12) is an electricity-discount artefact, NOT a KL rent decline. Do not use as R or as a rent turning-point instrument.

2024-01.what: CLASSIFICATION AND WEIGHT REVISION, NOT A REBASING. With the January 2024 release DOSM moved from COICOP 1999 (12 divisions, 4-digit detail; workbook sheet "4d_J20") to COICOP 2018 (13 divisions, 5-digit detail; sheet "5D_J23"). The 041 basket weight changed from 18.1 to 17.7 percent of the CPI.
2024-01.referenceBase: UNCHANGED at 2010=100 on both sides of the break.
2024-01.levelContinuity: NO level break in 041. The December 2023 index reads 132.4 in the December 2023 release (COICOP 1999) and 132.4 as the prior-month column of the January 2024 release (COICOP 2018). DOSM linked the series itself; we applied no splice factor and none is needed.
2024-01.linkFactorReason: Not applicable — the published levels are already continuous. Recording a link factor of 1.000 would imply we performed a splice; we did not.
2024-01.whatIsBroken: Comparability of the WEIGHTING STRUCTURE, and therefore of division-level aggregates, across 2023-12/2024-01. The 041 sub-index itself is a single expenditure class, so its own level and growth rate are unaffected.

pre-2010.what: No 3-digit or 4-digit CPI data before 2010-01 is published on OpenDOSM. cpi_3d and cpi_4d both start 2010-01. Only division 04 (cpi_2d) runs back to 1980-01.
pre-2010.effect: The rent series 041 begins 2010-01. Earlier DOSM CPI vintages used 2005=100 and 2000=100 reference bases with different baskets; those group-level series were not retrieved and are NOT reconstructed here.

repricingCadence.finding: The 041 monthly series is a QUARTERLY series carried forward. Across 197 month-on-month steps (2010-02 to 2026-06) the index changed in only 68 months. 66 of those 68 changes fall in the SECOND month of a calendar quarter (February, May, August, November); the only two exceptions are 2012-10 (-0.1) and 2013-12 (+0.1). Every one of the 66 quarters in the sample contains exactly one repricing, except 2013Q4 which contains two.
repricingCadence.implication: The monthly file carries no independent monthly information for rent. The effective observation count for the whole rent history is 66 quarterly observations, not 198 monthly ones. Any monthly-frequency lead/lag analysis on this series is measuring DOSM publication mechanics, not the rental market.
repricingCadence.quantisation: Published to 1 decimal on a level near 130-138, i.e. one tick = about 0.075 percent. A typical quarterly repricing is +0.3 to +0.7 index points = 4 to 9 ticks.

signHistory.yearOnYearNegative: 0 in 186 observations. Minimum YoY over the entire 2011-01 to 2026-06 record is +0.394 percent (2021-02).

validation.crossSourceCheck: The OpenDOSM parquet values for 041 were checked against the 041 row of the DOSM monthly release workbook (Jadual 23/25, sheet 5D) for four releases (2024-01, 2025-01, 2026-01, 2026-06), each supplying three months. 12/12 exact matches, no rounding differences.
validation.internalIdentity: 041 = 0411 = 04110 for all 198 months (cpi_3d group 041 and cpi_4d class 0411 are elementwise identical). Confirms 041 has a single leaf and no hidden sub-structure.
validation.coverage: cpi_041_national 198/198 months 2010-01..2026-06, no gaps, no nulls. State division-04 series 198/198 for all 16 states. Division 04 and headline national 558/558 months 1980-01..2026-06.
validation.anchorsNotAvailable: There is no second official Malaysian residential rent series to validate 041 against. The rent levels quoted in the trade press (for example "national average rent RM2,020/month", "KL RM2,901/month") come from private listing portals (IQI, PropertyGuru), are asking-price based, and are excluded by the project rule that asking is never the anchor. They are recorded in sourcesRejected and were NOT used to check anything.

officialAlternativesChecked.napicIndexCatalogue: NAPIC publishes five indices under "Indeks Harga dan Sewaan Harta Tanah" (Property Price and Rental Index): Indeks Harga Rumah Malaysia (MHPI, residential PRICE), Indeks Harga Pangsapuri Khidmat (IHPK, serviced apartment PRICE, archive years 2024-2026 only), Indeks Harga Kedai Lembah Klang (shop PRICE), Indeks Sewaan Pejabat Binaan Khas (PBO-RI, purpose-built office RENTAL), Indeks Sewaan Pusat Beli Belah (SC-RI, shopping centre RENTAL).
officialAlternativesChecked.conclusion: NAPIC publishes NO residential rental index. Both of its rental indices are commercial (office and shopping centre). Verified 2026-08-02 from https://napic.jpph.gov.my/archives/indeks-harga-dan-sewaan-harta-tanah.
officialAlternativesChecked.incidentalFinding: IHPK (Indeks Harga Pangsapuri Khidmat, serviced apartment price index) is a NEW NAPIC index whose archive only offers 2024-2026. It is a PRICE index, not rent, but it is the closest official thing to a KL high-rise price series and is therefore a candidate for the PRICE leg of forward-ledger 004 (F1). Not retrieved in this task.
officialAlternativesChecked.bnm: Bank Negara Malaysia publishes no rent index. Its housing statistics are prices (via NAPIC) and lending.

kl_rent_index.reason: DOSM publishes CPI by state only at DIVISION (2-digit) level. Group 041 exists for MALAYSIA only. State-level sub-division weights are not published, so KL 041 cannot be derived from KL 04. No other official source publishes a KL residential rent index.
kl_rent_index.doNotSubstitute: cpi_04_kl — it is 24 percent non-rent by weight and its 2020 movement is an electricity-tariff artefact.

high_rise_rent_index.reason: 041 is a single expenditure class (04110) with no dwelling-type split at any published digit. NAPIC has no residential rental index of any kind.

net_rent_R.reason: 041 is a gross contract-rent price index. It carries no level, no per-sq-ft denominator, and no deduction for management fee, quit rent/assessment, income tax, vacancy or collection loss. It supplies growth rates only. The level R required by four-quadrant NW (P = R/i) must come from elsewhere and is still 🔴.

new_letting_spot_rent.reason: No official series exists. CPI 041 prices continuing tenancies, so it is a stock-rent, not a spot-rent, measure. The only spot-rent data in Malaysia is listing (asking) data, which the project excludes.

f1Assessment.question: Can this series determine the rent turning-point timing required by forward-ledger entry 004 (F1)?
f1Assessment.verdict: NO — not as F1 is written. The series is usable for four-quadrant test 1 (rent GROWTH for g*), and is NOT usable for quarterly turning-point lead/lag against a price index.
reasons: Geography mismatch: F1 specifies KL high-rise. The only official rent series is NATIONAL and undifferentiated by dwelling type. National rent is dominated by the landed and low-rise rental stock that four-quadrant v1 section 7 explicitly rules out of the NE test.
Resolution: 66 quarterly observations with exactly one repricing per quarter; monthly detail is carry-forward. A "turn" can only be dated to the quarter, with zero redundancy for confirmation.

Structural lag: CPI 041 prices the stock of continuing tenancies. Malaysian residential tenancies are typically 1-2 year terms, so a change in market rent enters the index only as contracts renew. The index therefore lags spot rent by roughly the average remaining contract term, while MHPI is a transaction index that reflects spot. F1 asks whether rent turns at least one quarter BEFORE price; this pairing is mechanically biased AGAINST F1. A failed F1 read on this pairing would be uninterpretable — it cannot distinguish "the Lambda mechanism is false" from "the rent instrument lags by construction".

No turning points to date: over 2010-01 to 2026-06 the index has never posted a negative year-on-year change (minimum +0.394 percent) and posted a negative quarter only once (2020Q2, -0.079 percent on quarter averages). There is no historical turn to calibrate a turning-point rule against.

The in-sample window is empty: across 2022Q2-2023Q2 (OPR +125bp) 041 growth ACCELERATED — quarter-average QoQ 0.39 to 0.64 percent, quarter-average YoY 0.99 to 2.02 percent. National MHPI (data/prices.json, 206.8 at 2022Q2 to 214.3 at 2023Q2) also rose throughout. Neither leg turns, so the F1 in-sample first run cannot be executed at all — it is not merely in-sample-contaminated, it is undefined.
f1Assessment.tripwireNote: forward-ledger entry 004 tripwire 3 reads "DOSM CPI rental component year-on-year turns negative". On 186 year-on-year observations covering 2011-01 to 2026-06 this has never occurred, including through the 2020 COVID contraction and the 2022-2023 rate cycle. As written the tripwire is close to unreachable. This is reported as a fact about the instrument; the frozen ledger entry is NOT modified here.
whatWouldMakeF1Scorable: A KL high-rise rent series measured on NEW LETTINGS from an official or transaction-verified source. None exists today.
Tenancy registration data (a national tenancy act / rental deposit scheme has been proposed in Malaysia but not enacted); if enacted it would create the first official spot-rent record.

Failing both, F1 can only be restated in growth-rate-deceleration terms rather than level-turn terms, which is a change of judgement criterion and is FORBIDDEN under four-quadrant v1 section 1 revision rules for an already-frozen entry.
whatThisSeriesIsGoodFor: Four-quadrant test 1: g* comparison. Long-run nominal rent growth is well measured — 2010 to 2026 compound annual growth of the 041 index is available directly from the data block, and real rent growth can be computed against cpi_overall_national supplied here.
Sanity-checking any privately sourced KL rent growth claim: a private figure implying national-scale rent growth far above the 041 path is asking-side drift, not realised rent.

periods.monthly: 2010-01 .. 2026-06 for all 041-family series; 1980-01 .. 2026-06 for cpi_04_national and cpi_overall_national

derived.note: Computed by us from the published monthly values in the data block by simple arithmetic only. quarterAverage = mean of the three published months in the quarter. quarterEnd = the published value of the last month of the quarter. qoq/yoy = percentage change of quarterAverage against the previous quarter / same quarter previous year. NO interpolation, smoothing, seasonal adjustment or gap filling is involved; every input month is an officially published number.
derived.caution: Because the index reprices once per quarter in the middle month, quarterAverage and quarterEnd differ systematically. quarterEnd equals the repriced value of that quarter; quarterAverage is a two-thirds/one-third blend of the current and previous repricing. Pick one and state it — do not mix.
